records.subject: NEUROSCI
records.title: Meet Your Brain
records.description: Introduction to the brain and nervous system and how they are affected by your environment and everyday activities.

records.subject: NEUROSCI
records.title: Neuroscience Seminar
records.description: Introduces new students to individual faculty research interests and helps students link personal interests to academic majors.

records.subject: NEUROSCI
records.title: Art and the Brain
records.description: Explore networks involved in sensory perception; learn how art integrates perceptual experiences into works that affect our understanding of ourselves.

records.subject: NEUROSCI
records.title: Introduction to Communication in the Molecular Life Sciences
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: BIOLOGY 106 with a C or better or BIOLOGY 107 with a C or better.
records.description: Analysis of primary literature and an introduction to scientific communication skills in the molecular life sciences. Recommended preparation: Pre-admitted or admitted major in Biochemistry, Genetics & Cell Biology, Microbiology, or Neuroscience. (Crosslisted course offered as NEUROSCI 201, MBIOS 201.)

records.subject: NEUROSCI
records.title: Foundations of Neuroscience I
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: BIOLOGY 107.  Enrollment in NEUROSCI 301 not allowed if credit already earned for PSYCH 372.
records.description: Structure and function of the nervous system from single neurons to behavior.  Recommended preparation: CHEM 105, NEUROSCI 105.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: NEUROSCI
records.title: Foundations of Neuroscience II
records.description: In-depth concepts, analysis, and discussion of the experimental foundations for understanding nervous system function.  Recommended preparation: CHEM 105, CHEM 106.

records.subject: NEUROSCI
records.title: Neurons, Genes, and Behavior
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: NEUROSCI 301, 302, MBIOS 301, or PSYCH 372.
records.description: In-depth exploration of the organization of the brain, and how this organization underlies behavior.

records.subject: NEUROSCI
records.title: Foundations of Medical Physiology
records.description: Integrated functioning of organ systems, focusing on mechanisms of disease, organ dysfunction, and disturbances to whole-animal homeostasis and health.  (Crosslisted course offered as NEUROSCI 325, VET PH 325.)

records.subject: NEUROSCI
records.title: Foundations of Medical Physiology Lab
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: Concurrent enrollment in NEUROSCI 325 or VET PH 325.
records.description: Optional laboratory component of NEUROSCI/VET PH 325. Practical analysis of organ function and health using medical diagnostic equipment and clinical cases. (Crosslisted course offered as NEUROSCI 326, VET PH 326. Formerly NEUROSCI 426, VET PH 426.)
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: NEUROSCI
records.title: Techniques and Experimental Design in Neuroscience Research
records.description: Representative modern neuroscience experiments are explored from a conceptual, technical, and design perspective.

records.subject: NEUROSCI
records.title: Brain Matters: Critical Analysis in Neuroscience
records.description: Discussion and analysis of current trends in neuroscience and cutting-edge approaches to research.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: NEUROSCI
records.title: Cellular Neurobiology
records.description: Cellular and molecular interactions occurring within the nervous system. Recommended preparation: NEUROSCI 430.

records.subject: NEUROSCI
records.title: Neuroanatomy
records.description: Fundamental principles of the organization and plans of circuitry of the nervous system.

records.subject: NEUROSCI
records.title: Neuroanatomy Laboratory
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: NEUROSCI 301 or PSYCH 372; NEUROSCI 404 or concurrent enrollment or instructor permission.
records.description: Laboratory investigation of fundamental principles of the organization and plans of circuitry of the nervous system.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: NEUROSCI
records.title: Affective Neuroscience
records.description: Brain mechanisms of human and animal emotions. Credit not granted for both NEUROSCI 409 and NEUROSCI 509.

records.subject: NEUROSCI
records.title: Principles of Neurophysiology
records.description: Advanced exploration of the principles underlying cellular, sensory, motor and integrative functions of the nervous system.  Recommended preparation: previous or concurrent enrollment in PHYSICS 102 and 112, or PHYSICS 202 and 212, or PHYSICS 206.

records.subject: NEUROSCI
records.title: Principles of Neurophysiology Laboratory
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: NEUROSCI 301 or PSYCH 372; NEUROSCI 430 or concurrent enrollment or instructor permission.
records.description: Advanced laboratory exploration of the principles underlying cellular, sensory, motor, and integrative functions of the nervous system. Recommended preparation: MBIOS 303.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: NEUROSCI
records.title: Senior Project
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite:  Admitted to the major in Neuroscience; senior standing.
records.description: Senior capstone course for students majoring in Neuroscience.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: NEUROSCI
records.title: Senior Project-Poster
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: Admitted to the major in Neuroscience; senior standing.
records.description: Research project poster or oral presentation.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: NEUROSCI
records.title: Directed Research
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: Admitted to the major or minor in Neuroscience.
records.description: Introduction to neuroscience research literature.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: NEUROSCI
records.title: Special Topics
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: NEUROSCI 302 with a C or better or junior standing.
records.description: Reading, discussion, and exploration of contemporary topics in Neuroscience.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: NEUROSCI
records.title: Special Problems
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: By department permission only; admitted to the major or minor in Neuroscience.
records.description: Independent study conducted under the jurisdiction of an approving faculty member; may include independent research studies in technical or specialized problems; selection and analysis of specified readings; development of a creative project; or field experiences.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.
